items.title: Send these readings to your care team this week
items.text: Your average blood sugar was 178.3 mg/dL, and 10.9% of your readings were above 250 mg/dL. Contact your care team this week to discuss your readings.

items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: In real adults (CGMacros), a walk after a meal went with a rise only about 3.2 mg/dL smaller (95% CI -6.9 to 0.5): not distinguishable from zero. You walked after 0 of your scored meals, too few to measure your own effect yet. In the synthetic program, a walk after dinner went with a rise about 18.3 mg/dL smaller in the same person, more than after other meals (14.6 mg/dL). 10 to 19 minutes got most of the gain: 17.5 mg/dL less, against 19.5 for 20-29 minutes and 16.6 for 30+ minutes. If you take insulin or a sulfonylurea (glipizide, glyburide, glimepiride), ask your care team about low sugar before adding walks after meals.

rejected.text: Walking after a meal went with a rise about 3.2 mg/dL smaller in real adults. Walking 10 to 19 minutes after dinner may help, but ask your care team if you take insulin or a sulfonylurea.

items.title: Keep meal times steady around your shifts
items.text: You work nights, so clock-time rules about late dinners don't fit you. Keep your main meal at the same point in your waking day.

rejected.text: Keep your main meal at the same point in your waking day, since you work nights. This will help you establish a consistent routine.
